result.rationale: In AddGuestsDialog.tsx: `const message = `${err.data?.code}: ${t(err.message)}`;` — a template literal is always a non-empty string, so `showToast(message || t("unable_to_add_guests"), "error")` never falls back; if err.data/err.message are undefined, users see 'undefined: ...'. The fallback is dead code and the intended error message never shows.

adjudication.rationale: In `AddGuestsDialog.tsx` the `onError` handler does `const message = `${err.data?.code}: ${t(err.message)}`;` and then `showToast(message || t("unable_to_add_guests"), "error")`. A template literal always produces a string, so `message` will be truthy even if `err.data?.code` and/or `err.message` are `undefined`, resulting in a toast like `"undefined: undefined"` (or similar) and the fallback will never run. This is a real correctness issue introduced by the diff.
